newsitem.title: USA: IBM sets stock split, shares rise.
newsitem.headline: IBM sets stock split, shares rise.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp., aiming to give a boost to its recently battered stock, Tuesday set a 2-for-1 split that helped fuel a rally in one of the most widely held stocks.
The world's biggest computer maker said its board had approved the split subject to shareholders approving an increase in the number of authorised common shares.

IBM's stock, which had tumbled since the company last week reported fourth quarter earnings that disappointed Wall Street, bounced back and rose $7.25 to $153 in active New York Stock Exchange trading.
The stock is widely held by individual and institutional investors worldwide and is one of 30 issues in the Dow Jones industrial average.

Not all of the jump was due to the announcement of the split. The stock rose early in the session after a government report on wages in the fourth quarter helped calm inflation jitters on Wall Street.
But the stock rose another $1.50 or so after IBM announced the split, which is scheduled to take effect in May.
"It's mainly a psychological move," said Daniel Ries at Nomura Securities.
"I suppose it makes the stock more affordable to smaller retail accounts who don't want to shell out $15,000 for 100 shares of IBM stock, but in terms of institutional investors it has no impact."
The rise in IBM accounted for about 23 points of the Dow industrials' 83-point surge.
Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones upgraded his rating on the stock to strong buy from buy but did not comment further.
Before its reported earnings last week, IBM's share price had doubled in the last year or so.
But after it said last Tuesday that earnings rose 18 percent to $2 billion, or $3.93 a share, in the quarter, the stock took a dive, falling about 22 points over four sessions.
Several analysts cut ratings on the stock after the earnings report, citing sluggish mainframe sales, weakness in Europe and other factors.

Although the slide in IBM's stock price appeared to be over for now, analysts said the shares would not break out of the current range until there were signs that IBM's mainframe sales were starting to improve.
"I wouldn't look for a meaningful move in the stock until they in some way reassure investors that hardware (revenues) will grow in the 8 percent range," Nomura's Ries said.

The company said the board proposed raising the number of authorised common shares to 1.875 billion from 750 million. It said the record date for the split was May 9 and that the split shares will be distributed on May 27.
It also said its annual shareholders meeting will be held on April 29 in Dallas.
